content.text: The renewal mechanics meet the preferred position, so no redline is needed.

input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: § 8.2 and § 8.3 match the preferred position in every parameter: renewal terms are twelve months (not multi-year); Customer may opt out on thirty days' written notice (≤ 30 days, and the deadline is extended if Vendor misses its reminder); Vendor must send a renewal reminder at least sixty days before renewal; and renewal uplift is capped at the lesser of CPI over the preceding twelve months and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods. The only asymmetry is that non-renewal is Customer's right alone, which favours us. § 2.1's three-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" could blunt the practical value of the opt-out, but that is a minimum-commitment/termination-rights issue addressed under the relevant commitment rule rather than a defect in the renewal mechanics, so no renewal redline is proposed.
